metadata.case_name: Arab Spring: Tunisia vs Egypt vs Libya
metadata.author: transcribed from live/runs by expansion agent
metadata.key_test: P1 + rentier (Safeguard E): Libya's high HDI/GDP (oil-inflated) would predict resilience, but the rentier flag should invert this to 'fragile, will fragment on shock'; and Safeguard C reversal risk for both democratic transitions (Tunisia and Egypt) with weak economic delivery.
metadata.notes: Arab Spring (post-2011) shock. Pre-event 2010. CPI 2010 figures are EXACT (Transparency International official CPI 2010 dataset) and are placed in indicators; Libya's 2010 total natural-resource rents (53.663% of GDP, World Bank 'The Changing Wealth of Nations' via CEIC) are placed in indicators. WGI ordering Tunisia > Egypt > Libya is high-confidence but exact 2010 percentile ranks were not isolated; those pillar values remain ordinal estimates. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

Tunisia.notes: 2010 estimate (ordinal): P1 highest of the trio, balanced, low rents -> MI highest of three, narrowest spread. WGI Rule of Law highest of three; Govt Effectiveness best (~+0.4 band). CPI 2010 = 4.3 (rank 66) -- EXACT, placed in indicator. HDI 2010 high-medium; GDP per cap PPP 2010 ~$10-11k (approximate range, left null); resource rents low; political stability moderate. Democratic transition + weak P4 -> HIGH reversal risk (Safeguard C). WGI pillar values are estimates (exact 2010 percentiles not isolated); pre-2012 CPI is ordinal-cross-country only. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

data_sources.wgi: World Bank WGI (2010, ordinal; exact percentile ranks not isolated)

Egypt.notes: 2010 estimate (ordinal): P1 low-moderate, large population, military-economy distortion -> MI low (matches dataset: 2012 M=-0.008, near floor; 2024 P1=0.297). WGI Rule of Law middle (mildly negative); Govt Effectiveness negative by 2010. CPI 2010 = 3.1 (rank 105) -- EXACT, placed in indicator. HDI 2010 medium; GDP per cap PPP 2010 ~$10k (approximate, left null); resource rents moderate; political stability low. Democratic transition + weak delivery -> HIGH reversal risk (Safeguard C); military-dominant (Safeguard G Tier 1). WGI pillar values are estimates; pre-2012 CPI ordinal-cross-country only. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

context.growth_trajectory: oil-inflated apparent wealth over an institutional vacuum

data_sources.cpi: Transparency International official CPI 2010 dataset (2.2, rank 154, 0-10 scale)
data_sources.resource_rents: World Bank 'The Changing Wealth of Nations' via CEIC (2010 oil rents 52.785%; total natural-resource rents 53.663% of GDP)
data_sources.wgi: World Bank WGI (2010, ordinal; exact percentile ranks not isolated)

Libya.notes: 2010 estimate (ordinal): P1 bottom (near-global-worst), P4 massively distorted by ~53% rents (rentier capture inflating apparent wealth/P1) -> MI low despite high GDP; widest pillar spread (oil wealth vs institutional vacuum). WGI Rule of Law bottom; Govt Effectiveness bottom. CPI 2010 = 2.2 (rank 154) -- EXACT, placed in indicator. Resource rents: oil 52.785%, total 53.663% of GDP -- EXACT, placed in indicator (resource_rents_pct_gdp). HDI 2010 highest nominal (oil-inflated); GDP per cap PPP 2010 ~$12,800 (oil; approximate, left null); political stability low-moderate (police state). Safeguard E bidirectional flag: rents far above the 25-30% threshold both inflated apparent stability under Gaddafi AND left no institutional substrate on regime collapse -> catastrophic fragmentation predicted. WGI pillar values are estimates; pre-2012 CPI ordinal-cross-country only. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Libya = P4 resource distortion + P1 vacuum (rentier collapse); Egypt = P1 + military capture; Tunisia = P4 weak delivery driving reversal.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias

Tunisia.outcome_summary: Best of the three: kept a functioning, undivided state and a decade of democracy (2011-2021), then the Saied self-coup (July 2021); autocratizing but intact state. V-Dem codes Tunisia an electoral democracy 2012-2021, reverting to electoral autocracy in 2022.
key_events: Saied self-coup July 2021 (Article 80; parliament suspended, PM dismissed)

Egypt.outcome_summary: Restabilized as an autocracy with intact institutions; 2013 military coup + Rabaa massacre (~900-1,000 killed in a single day per Human Rights Watch). 2024 P1 = 0.297.

Libya.outcome_summary: Failed/fragmented state: NTC -> 2014 civil war resumes (rival governments) -> divided (GNA/Haftar) -> still fragmented, no unified state as of 2024. 62.1% GDP contraction in the 2011 civil war; 2024 per-capita PPP GDP only 65% of its pre-war 2010 level (IMF via Wikipedia 'Economy of Libya').

result_coding_reference.coding_rule: When ambiguous between confirmed and partial, code PARTIAL. When ambiguous between partial and falsified, code PARTIAL but note ambiguity.

analysis.overall_assessment: The clearest 'P1 + rentier' confirmation in the set; all applicable predictions CONFIRMED. Without Safeguard E, Libya's high HDI/GDP would have predicted resilience; the rentier flag correctly inverts this to 'fragile, will fragment on shock.' The case also shows the framework's directional honesty: it predicted Tunisia relatively best, not Tunisia good -- and Tunisia's democracy did reverse (Safeguard C).
safeguards_triggered: C (Tunisia & Egypt reversal risk -- both HIGH)
G (Egypt Tier 1 military; Tunisia Tier 2 legal/institutional)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Rentier capture (Safeguard E) must be applied bidirectionally: high P4 from rents is a vulnerability, not a strength, once a regime shock arrives. Libya (53.663% rents in 2010) confirms this -- the regime fell with no indigenous administrative capacity and the country fragmented.
proposed_framework_modifications: Apply Safeguard E bidirectionally and explicitly invert resilience predictions when rents exceed ~30% of GDP.
analysis.baseline_impact: None degrading; reinforces Safeguard E. No baseline-breaking modification proposed.
analysis.strict_recode_note: Strict re-code applied per run6 (post-hoc d-dimension -> PARTIAL; narrow-gap a-trajectory annotated with Mod4). Honest aggregate target ~62-78%.
